content: 1. In 2016, Delamanid was provided to five patients at a hospital through the Otsuka company. 2. Lawrence Mbuagbaw conducted a biostatistical consultation to support FDA reporting requirements for the use of Bedaquiline for Janssen Pharmaceuticals, for which he received payment. 3. Anuj K. Bhatnagar is the Co-Principal Investigator for the STREAM 2 trial at the Rajan Babu Institute of Pulmonary Medicine and Tuberculosis (RBI PMT) in Delhi, India. This trial began at the site in March 2019. 4. The financial aspects of the STREAM 2 trial are managed by Vital Strategies, an affiliate of the International Union Against Tuberculosis and Lung Disease (IUATLD). This includes ward refurbishment, equipment procurement, staff hiring, laboratory upgrades, access to laboratory tests, and patient support, including monetary compensation. No funds were transferred directly to the institute for this trial. 5. The National Institute for Research in Tuberculosis (NIRT) in Chennai, under the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR), initiated a Phase 3 trial called BEAT TB to evaluate the efficacy and tolerability of newer drug combinations for pre-XDR and XDR-TB across five sites in India. 6. At the RBI PMT site, where Dr. Bhatnagar is the Principal Investigator for the BEAT TB trial, a site initiation visit and recruitment of personnel have been completed. 7. The first installment of the grant for the BEAT TB trial by NIRT Chennai was allocated for staff recruitment, equipment, laboratory reagents, and patient and DOT provider support. 8. Amrita Daftary provided qualitative expertise for designing and evaluating an adherence intervention for XDR-TB-HIV patients in South Africa (2016–2021). She also conducted qualitative research for the current GDG meeting. 9. Amrita Daftary completed a study at McGill University (2015–2018) to engage pharmacy providers in India for TB screening and referral. She also conducted an observational study in South Africa (2017–2020) to assess the quality of clinical care for TB diagnosis. 10. David Dowdy received a research grant from the Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation (BMGF) for his institution, totaling approximately $300,000, with $50,000 as his current year interest. He also received $10,000 for travel to attend meetings funded by BMGF. 11. Gabriela Gomez provided modeling results for an investment case on a universal TB drug regimen, funded by BMGF ($40,000, concluded in 2018). She managed a research grant for an economic evaluation of TB-PRACTECAL funded by MSF (~£150,000). She also conducted an economic evaluation of the BPaL regimen funded by the TB Alliance (~£60,000). 12. Gabriela Gomez has been employed by Sanofi Pasteur since August 2019, leading vaccine epidemiology and modeling in Europe. She clarified that Sanofi Pasteur currently has no TB vaccine in its commercial pipeline. 13. Richard Menzies conducted WHO-commissioned evidence reviews (2016–present) to synthesize evidence for MDR-TB treatment guidelines. 14. Rada Savic received research funding from NIH, UNITAID, and BMGF for her institution (UCSF), where she is a principal investigator. She serves on the Scientific Advisory Committee for the TB Alliance without receiving income for this role. 15. Zarir Udwadia supported approximately 40 patients in accessing Bedaquiline and three patients in accessing Delamanid through compassionate use programs by Janssen and Otsuka, respectively, without charging fees or financial transactions with manufacturers. 16. Andrew Vernon leads a clinical research group at the US CDC conducting TB trials, including studies on rifapentine and levofloxacin. His branch has supported studies on drug-susceptible TB and enrollment in the Opti-Q study, which evaluates levofloxacin doses for DR-TB treatment. 17. Gary Maartens declared that his laboratory will receive $218,460 from NIH for drug assays in a trial on the safety and pharmacokinetics of Bedaquiline and Delamanid in MDR-TB treatment. He will not receive salary support. 18. WHO conducted a public notice to allow comments on potential competing interests that may have been overlooked during earlier assessments. 19. All members of the Guideline Development Group (GDG) and Evidence Review Group (ERG) completed WHO Declaration of Interest forms and agreed to confidentiality. The WHO Guideline Steering Committee reviewed these forms to ensure neutrality and independence. 20. Five GDG members declared non-significant interests that did not affect the neutrality of the guideline development process, allowing their full participation. 21. Farhana Amanullah declared her roles as a pediatric TB expert for WHO, Harvard Medical School, and the Global Fund, with associated funding. 22. Tsira Chakhai declared her roles as a research coordinator for TB Alliance clinical trials and community engagement projects.
